name: auth-gateway-resolveHomeRedirect
hook: Use resolveHomeRedirect in page.tsx for auth-aware routing
body:
When a /start page serves both authenticated and unauthenticated users, restore the auth gateway pattern from home/page.tsx: call getMeUser(), check COURSE_ID_COOKIE_NAME, call resolveHomeRedirect(), redirect if destination !== '/start'.

Why: The previous PR removed this logic, creating a BLOCK regression where authenticated users with a selected course would land on /start instead of being redirected to /study.

How to apply: See src/app/(frontend)/start/page.tsx for the exact pattern — getMeUser() + cookies() + resolveHomeRedirect() + redirect().
why: Auth routing regressions are silent and high-impact; the auth gateway must always be preserved in page route files.

name: lucide-icon-component-type
hook: Correct TypeScript type for lucide-react icon components
body:
When using lucide-react icons as component types (e.g. in a Feature data structure), the correct type is:

  import type { ForwardRefExoticComponent, RefAttributes, SVGProps } from 'react'
  type LucideIconComponent = ForwardRefExoticComponent<
    Omit<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, 'ref'> & RefAttributes<SVGSVGElement>
  >

Do NOT use 'Icon' from lucide-react (it doesn't exist as a type). Do NOT use 'typeof Icon'.

Why: lucide-react exports ForwardRefExoticComponent-based icons. The IconNode/Icon interface is internal.

How to apply: See src/app/(frontend)/start/_components/NewStartPage/features-data.ts for usage.
why: Using 'Icon' as a type causes TS2749: 'Icon' refers to a value, not a type. The ForwardRefExoticComponent type is the correct programmatic type for lucide icons.

name: body-class-landing-page
hook: Document body class side effects with a comment
body:
When using document.body.classList.add('landing-page') to hide header/footer, add a comment explaining what the class does and where it is defined.

Why: 'landing-page' is a side effect that is invisible in the component tree and easy to accidentally break. The comment in NewStartPage now explains it's defined in globals.css.

How to apply: Add a comment like '// .landing-page body class hides site header/footer (defined in globals.css)' before the useEffect.
why: Without documentation, future developers may remove this useEffect assuming it's dead code.
